item.title: An Overview of Context Engineering for Knowledge Workers
item.description: In this episode, I’m joined by Eleanor Berger, AI Leadership Expert and Founder at Agentic Ventures, for a practical overview of Context Engineering and why it matters for knowledge workers. We break down what context engineering really is, how it differs from prompt engineering, and how business professionals, domain experts, and team leaders can use it to get more reliable, repeatable, and higher-quality results from AI systems. Drawing on Eleanor’s experience advising hundreds of organizations and leading AI transformation efforts, this conversation focuses on moving from clever experiments to AI workflows that actually support real work and real decisions.

As a domain expert, you already know what tools are missing, which workflows are inefficient, and what users actually need. The challenge is not knowing what to build. It is turning that knowledge into something tangible.

AI lets you do that directly. By clearly describing your goals, constraints, and expected outcomes, you can guide AI to create prototypes, tools, and workflows that reflect how work really happens in your domain. With structure and intentional planning, AI handles the technical execution while you stay focused on shaping solutions based on your expertise.

Spec Driven Development (SDD) is an approach where you and AI start by clearly defining what you want to build before generating anything. It focuses on making your intent explicit through goals, requirements, constraints, and examples so AI understands the problem space upfront.

For domain experts, this means capturing what you already know about users, workflows, and outcomes, then using that clarity to guide AI. The result is less rework, more consistent output, and prototypes, tools, or workflows that better reflect how things should actually work in your domain.

Vibe coding is the practice of using AI to quickly turn ideas into prototypes, tools, and workflows through conversation and iteration, without needing to write the code yourself.

As a domain expert and knowledge worker, you should care because it lets you apply your expertise directly. Instead of waiting on engineering cycles or learning a full tech stack, you can explore ideas, validate assumptions, and build useful artifacts faster. When paired with clear goals and basic structure, vibe coding becomes a practical way for knowledge workers to adapt to the new baseline where domain expertise and AI work together.

With AI, you can build the things you already know should exist in your domain. That includes prototypes to test ideas, internal tools that remove manual work, and workflows that automate repetitive or error-prone tasks.

Domain experts commonly use AI to create planning tools, decision support aids, content and data pipelines, dashboards, internal utilities, and early versions of applications used to validate needs with real users.

Want to see some great apps built using AI? Check out our App Gallery!

AI is powerful, but it does not understand your domain, your users, or your constraints unless you make those things explicit. As a domain expert, your value comes from knowing what matters, what does not, and how decisions affect real outcomes.

Knowing how to guide AI means translating that understanding into clear instructions, context, and expectations. When you do that, AI becomes an extension of your expertise. You get more accurate results, fewer misfires, and outputs that align with real-world needs instead of generic answers.

item.title: Galactic Invaders
item.description:
About

A 2D retro-style space shooter where you protect your city from incoming waves of aliens. Shoot them down, earn temporary rapid-fire during bonus moments, and unlock nukes as your score increases. The goal is straightforward: stay alive and keep the city safe.

How to Play

  1. Use ←, ↑, →, ↓ or [WASD] to move your spaceship
  2. Press [Space] to shoot
  3. Press [Q] to activate the nuke (when available)
  4. Press [M] to toggle sound on/off
  5. Destroy aliens to earn points
  6. Avoid getting hit by aliens.
  7. Stop the aliens from destroying your city.
  8. Try to achieve the highest score possible!

Features

  • Smooth player movement with keyboard controls
  • Dynamic shooting mechanics
  • Progressive difficulty with increasing alien waves
  • Score tracking and lives system
  • Sound effects and visual feedback
  • Special nuke power-up to clear the screen
  • Scrolling starfield background for immersive space atmosphere

Game Play Controls

  • ←, ↑, →, ↓ or [WASD] : Move
  • [Space] : Shoot
  • [Q] : Activate nuke (when available)
  • [M] : Toggle sound on/off

item.title: I Build with AI Website
item.description:
About

First site I’ve built from scratch using vibe coding techniques. After relying on tools like Wix and Framer, I wanted full control over what I create. It’s also my first time using the Hugo SSG framwework, and I’m quickly seeing the benefits of static site generators: fast performance, a lightweight codebase, and clean, responsive output.

Technology Stack

  • Hugo : Static site generator with custom theme architecture
  • SCSS/Sass : Modular CSS preprocessing with design system variables and mixins
  • HTML5 : Semantic markup with Hugo templating engine
  • CSS Grid & Flexbox : Modern layout systems for responsive design
  • Hugo Pipes : Asset processing pipeline for SCSS compilation and minification
  • Markdown : Content authoring with front matter configuration
  • Git : Version control and GitHub Pages deployment
  • GitHub Pages : Static site hosting and continuous deployment
  • Custom Design System : Component-based CSS architecture with utility classes
  • Responsive Design : Mobile-first approach with consistent breakpoints
  • CSS Custom Properties : Dynamic theming and runtime style management
  • Hugo Taxonomies : Content organization and navigation structure

Tools Used

  • Cursor
  • Claude Code
  • Cursor Chat (with Claude 4 Sonnet, Gemini Flash 2.5, Deepseek-v3.1)
  • Gemini Code Assist / CLI
  • ChatGPT
  • Claude Desktop
  • Repo Prompt

item.title: TreeX
item.description:
About

TreeX is a cross-platform CLI tool for visualizing and exporting folder structures. It provides emoji-based directory trees with extensive export capabilities to multiple formats text documents and images.

Features

  • 📤 Multi-Format Export - SVG, PNG, WebP, and Markdown with perfect emoji rendering
  • ⚡ Smart Filtering - Configurable ignore lists and display options
  • 🔍 Detailed Information - File permissions, hidden file detection and more
  • 🎯 Flexible Output - Console display or export to files
  • 🌍 Cross-Platform - Works on Windows, macOS, and Linux
  • 🎨 Emoji Management - Customize folder, file, and status emojis with easy list, update, and restore
